ei.title: Chapter 0-QN35 1번: The Power of a Teacher's Voice
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others (A)[recognise / ignore] the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a (B)[positive / negative] class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very (C)[useful / useless] when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 목소리의 힘을 인식하다, 긍정적인 반응, 매우 유용한
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignore — positive — useful (A 반대: 인식하다→무시하다)
✅ ② recognise — positive — useful — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ recognise — negative — useful (B 반대: 긍정적인→부정적인)
❌ ④ recognise — positive — useless (C 반대: 유용한→쓸모없는)
det.tip: recognise(인식하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다), useful(유용한) ↔ useless(쓸모없는)

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to (A)[control / lose] your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more (B)[confidently / hesitantly] you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly and avoid shouting as much as possible. A (C)[quiet / loud], authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 목소리를 조절하다, 자신 있게 지시하다, 조용한 어조
det.analysis:
❌ ① lose — confidently — quiet (A 반대: 조절하다→잃다)
❌ ② control — hesitantly — quiet (B 반대: 자신 있게→머뭇거리며)
✅ ③ control — confidently — quiet — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ control — confidently — loud (C 반대: 조용한→시끄러운)
det.tip: control(조절하다) ↔ lose(잃다), confidently(자신 있게) ↔ hesitantly(머뭇거리며)

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a (A)[great / poor] skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly (B)[sparingly / frequently] and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and (C)[measured / reckless] tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 훌륭한 기술, 아껴서 사용하다, 침착한 어조
det.analysis:
✅ ① great — sparingly — measured — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② poor — sparingly — measured (A 반대: 훌륭한→형편없는)
❌ ③ great — frequently — measured (B 반대: 아껴서→자주)
❌ ④ great — sparingly — reckless (C 반대: 침착한→무모한)
det.tip: sparingly(아껴서) ↔ frequently(자주), measured(침착한) ↔ reckless(무모한)

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the ①<u>power</u> of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to ②<u>develop</u> as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a ③<u>noisy</u> classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly and ④<u>encourage</u> shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① power(힘) ✅ / ② develop(발달시키다) ✅ / ③ noisy(시끄러운) ✅ / ④ encourage(장려하다) ❌ → avoid(피하다)가 원문
det.analysis:
① power(힘): 인간 목소리의 힘 — 적절 ✅
② develop(발달시키다): 발달시켜야 할 기술 — 적절 ✅
③ noisy(시끄러운): 시끄러운 교실을 뚫고 나가다 — 적절 ✅
④ encourage(장려하다): 원문은 avoid(피하다). 고함치는 것을 최대한 '피하라'는 조언인데 '장려하라'는 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: avoid(피하다) ↔ encourage(장려하다). 고함은 피하라는 것이 글의 조언

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others ①<u>ignore</u> the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to ②<u>control</u> your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very ③<u>useful</u> when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, ④<u>authoritative</u> and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① ignore(무시하다) ❌ → recognise(인식하다)가 원문 / ② control(조절하다) ✅ / ③ useful(유용한) ✅ / ④ authoritative(권위 있는) ✅
det.analysis:
① ignore(무시하다): 원문은 recognise(인식하다). 배우·가수 등은 목소리의 힘을 '인식한다'는 것이 문맥인데 '무시한다'는 정반대 ←정답
② control(조절하다): 목소리를 조절하는 법을 배우다 — 적절 ✅
③ useful(유용한): 목소리를 크게 내는 것이 유용하다 — 적절 ✅
④ authoritative(권위 있는): 권위 있고 침착한 어조 — 적절 ✅
det.tip: recognise(인식하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다)

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class ①<u>response</u>. There are times when being able to project your voice ②<u>loudly</u> will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your ③<u>softest</u> voice incredibly sparingly and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly ④<u>panicked</u> shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① response(반응) ✅ / ② loudly(크게) ✅ / ③ softest(가장 부드러운) ❌ → loudest(가장 큰)가 원문 / ④ panicked(당황한) ✅
det.analysis:
① response(반응): 긍정적인 학급 반응 — 적절 ✅
② loudly(크게): 목소리를 크게 내는 것 — 적절 ✅
③ softest(가장 부드러운): 원문은 loudest(가장 큰). 아주 아껴 써야 하는 것은 '가장 큰' 목소리이지 '가장 부드러운' 목소리가 아님 ←정답
④ panicked(당황한): 약간 당황한 듯한 고함 — 적절 ✅
det.tip: loudest(가장 큰) ↔ softest(가장 부드러운). 큰 목소리를 아껴 쓰라는 조언

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자신 있게 지시할수록 긍정적인 반응의 가능성이 높아진다
det.analysis:
❌ ① negative(부정적인): 자신 있게 지시하는데 부정적 반응이 커진다는 것은 문맥 모순
✅ ② positive(긍정적인): 더 자신 있게 지시할수록 긍정적 반응 가능성이 높아짐 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ random(무작위의): 지시의 자신감과 무관
❌ ④ delayed(지연된): 반응의 성질(긍정/부정)이 아닌 시점, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: a positive class response = 긍정적인 학급 반응

det.korean: 조용하고 침착한 어조가 고함보다 훨씬 더 큰 영향을 준다
det.analysis:
❌ ① noise(소음): 조용한 어조가 더 큰 '소음'을 준다는 것은 모순
❌ ② confusion(혼란): 침착한 어조의 효과로 혼란은 부적절
❌ ③ silence(침묵): '더 많은 침묵'은 문맥상 어색
✅ ④ impact(영향, 효과): 조용하고 침착한 어조가 고함보다 훨씬 더 큰 효과를 냄 — 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: have so much more impact = 훨씬 더 큰 영향(효과)을 주다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 목소리 조절은 초임 교사가 발달시켜야 할 가장 중요한 기술 중 하나다
det.analysis:
✅ ① important(중요한): 뒤에 그 이점들이 이어지므로 발달시켜야 할 '중요한' 기술 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② optional(선택적인): '가장 ~한 기술 중 하나'라는 강조와 어긋남
❌ ③ confusing(혼란스러운): 기술을 혼란스럽다고 표현하는 것은 부적절
❌ ④ temporary(일시적인): 발달시켜야 할 기술의 성질로 부적절
det.tip: one of the most important skills = 가장 중요한 기술 중 하나

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 useful와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: useful = 유용한, 도움이 되는
det.analysis:
❌ ① harmful(해로운): useful의 반의어 방향
❌ ② boring(지루한): 유용성과 무관한 성질
✅ ③ helpful(도움이 되는): useful과 동의어 — 도움이 되는 ←정답
❌ ④ difficult(어려운): 난이도이지 유용성이 아님
det.tip: useful = helpful = beneficial (유용한, 도움이 되는)

det.korean: sparingly = 아껴서, 드물게
det.analysis:

❌ ② generously(아낌없이): 아껴 쓰는 것과 반대
❌ ③ constantly(끊임없이): 아껴 쓰는 것과 반대
✅ ④ seldom(좀처럼 ~않게, 드물게): sparingly와 동의어 — 큰 목소리를 아주 드물게 씀 ←정답
det.tip: sparingly = seldom = rarely (아껴서, 드물게)

det.analysis:

✅ ② deliberate(신중한, 의도적인): measured와 동의어 — 신중하고 절제된 ←정답
❌ ③ careless(부주의한): 신중함과 반대
❌ ④ loud(시끄러운): 어조의 크기이지 신중함이 아님
det.tip: measured = deliberate = controlled (신중한, 침착한)

det.korean: authoritative = 권위 있는, 확신에 찬 ↔ submissive = 순종적인, 고분고분한
det.analysis:

questions.passage:
(A) When working in a noisy classroom, being able to <u>project</u> your voice loudly is a very useful skill for a teacher.

(B) The engineers worked on a huge construction <u>project</u> for over two years before it was finally completed.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 project의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) project = (목소리를) 멀리 내보내다(동사) / (B) project = 계획, 사업, 프로젝트(명사)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 계획, 사업 — (B) (목소리를) 내보내다: (A)(B) 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
❌ ② (A) 예상하다 — (B) 튀어나오다: (A)는 예상이 아닌 목소리를 내보냄
✅ ③ (A) (목소리를) 내보내다 — (B) 계획, 사업: (A)는 목소리를 멀리 내보내다, (B)는 건설 프로젝트 ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 투영하다 — (B) 추정하다: (B)는 명사 '사업'이지 동사가 아님
det.tip: project: (목소리를) 내보내다(v.) / 계획·사업(n.)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to tell someone what you think they should do, especially because you have more knowledge or experience"

det.korean: 더 많은 지식·경험을 바탕으로 무엇을 해야 할지 말해 주다 = advise(조언하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① recognise(인식하다): 알아차리는 것이지 조언이 아님
✅ ② advise(조언하다): 무엇을 해야 할지 말해 주다 — 정의 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ project(내보내다): 목소리를 내보내는 것, 조언과 무관
❌ ④ control(조절하다): 통제하는 것이지 조언이 아님
det.tip: advise = to recommend, to counsel (조언하다)

questions.passage: The more __________ (confident) you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: confident(형용사: 자신 있는) → confidently(부사: 자신 있게)
det.analysis: 빈칸은 동사 give를 수식하는 자리이므로 부사가 필요. 형용사 confident를 부사 confidently로 어형 변환. 'The more confidently you give instructions' = 더 자신 있게 지시할수록
det.tip: confident(adj. 자신 있는) → confidently(adv. 자신 있게): 동사를 수식할 땐 부사

questions.passage: There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and __________ (know) that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: know(동사: 알다) → knowing(동명사: 아는 것)
det.analysis: 빈칸은 뒤의 'is a great skill'의 주어 자리이므로 동명사가 필요. 동사 know를 동명사 knowing으로 바꿔 '~을 아는 것'이라는 주어를 만듦. 'knowing that you can cut through ... is a great skill' = ~을 뚫고 나갈 수 있다는 것을 아는 것은 훌륭한 기술이다
det.tip: 주어 자리의 동사 → 동명사(-ing). know → knowing (아는 것)

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can __________, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 목소리를 크게 내어 시끄러운 교실을 뚫고 나갈 수 있다는 것은 훌륭한 기술이다
det.analysis:
✅ ① cut through a noisy classroom(시끄러운 교실을 뚫고 나가다): 목소리를 크게 투사해 소음을 뚫는 능력 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② whisper in a silent library(조용한 도서관에서 속삭이다): 목소리를 크게 내는 문맥과 정반대
❌ ③ sit quietly in a classroom(교실에 조용히 앉다): 목소리 투사 능력과 무관
❌ ④ hide behind a classroom door(교실 문 뒤에 숨다): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: cut through a noisy classroom = 시끄러운 교실을 (목소리로) 뚫고 나가다

questions.passage: Actors, singers, politicians and countless others recognise the power of the human voice as a means of communication beyond the simple decoding of the words that are used. Learning to control your voice and use it for different purposes is, therefore, one of the most important skills to develop as an early career teacher. The more confidently you give instructions, the higher the chance of a positive class response. There are times when being able to project your voice loudly will be very useful when working in school, and knowing that you can cut through a noisy classroom, dinner hall or playground is a great skill to have. However, I would always advise that you __________ and avoid shouting as much as possible. A quiet, authoritative and measured tone has so much more impact than slightly panicked shouting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그러나 나는 항상 가장 큰 목소리를 아주 아껴 쓰고 고함은 최대한 피하라고 조언한다
det.analysis:
❌ ① shout at your students constantly(학생들에게 끊임없이 고함치다): 뒤의 'avoid shouting'과 정반대
❌ ② raise your voice at every opportunity(기회마다 목소리를 높이다): 아껴 쓰라는 조언과 모순
❌ ③ speak as loudly as you possibly can(가능한 한 크게 말하다): 고함을 피하라는 조언과 모순
✅ ④ use your loudest voice incredibly sparingly(가장 큰 목소리를 아주 아껴 쓰다): 'However'로 이어지며 고함을 피하라는 조언과 일치 ←정답
det.tip: However + avoid shouting → 큰 목소리는 아껴 쓰라는 것이 핵심 조언
